clue.text: Dish, a strong concoction going bad

indicators.note: a concoction is something mixed up, so the letters of 'a strong' are stirred into a new order

parts.note: food going bad is said to be going off

explanation.surface: A powerful brew that has started to turn sour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going bad' looks like part of the dish's description, but it is the slang for food that has spoiled; 'concoction' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef stroganoff is a Russian dish of beef strips in a sour-cream sauce.

clue.text: Sidney accepted fifty young fish

indicators.note: something accepted is taken in, so the short name holds the numeral inside it

parts.note: Sid is the usual short form of the name Sidney
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A man called Sidney takes in fifty little fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Sild are young herring, often canned like sardines in Scandinavia.

clue.text: Optimistic girl

definitions.meaning: hopeful, seeing things through a cheerful lens

explanation.definitionFit: A rosy outlook is a hopeful one; Rosy is also a female forename.

clue.text: Caper by heartless mob behind bars

indicators.note: behind bars means locked up inside, so the prison word holds the other letters within it

parts.note: bars stand for a prison, and gaol is the British spelling of jail

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of 'mob' is removed, keeping only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A prank pulled by a ruthless gang who end up in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind bars' reads as one phrase meaning jailed; split it, 'behind' is the container signal and 'bars' is the prison, spelt the British way.
explanation.definitionFit: To gambol is to skip or frolic playfully, which is also to caper.

clue.text: Abstinence on a national scale

parts.note: abstinence suggests refusing drink or pleasure, but here it is a whole country refraining from meddling in other states' affairs

explanation.surface: A whole country giving up drink or vice together.
explanation.definitionFit: A policy of keeping out of other nations' conflicts is a state's refraining from involvement.

clue.text: Healthier mechanic

definitions.meaning: a tradesman who assembles or installs machinery

explanation.definitionFit: Being in better shape makes one more fit; an engineering tradesman who assembles parts is also called by this name.

clue.text: In the log put something about old secret police

indicators.note: In tells us the answer sits inside the run of letters in 'log put'

explanation.surface: Some note entered into a logbook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals the letters hidden in 'log put'; 'something about' is padding that only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The OGPU was the Soviet political police agency of the 1920s and early 1930s, forerunner of the NKVD and KGB.

clue.text: Attacking something aggressively pursuing one's goal

definitions.meaning: throwing oneself into a task with full energy

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes both an all-out attack on a task and chasing a target with determination.

clue.text: Bud reading version that is full-length

indicators.note: a version is a rendering in a different form, so the letters of 'Bud reading' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A friend called Bud reading the complete edition of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version' rearranges BUD READING into the answer; 'that is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An unabridged text is complete, not shortened, so it is the full-length edition.

clue.text: Does it come at the end of the eleventh hour?…

definitions.text: Does it come at the end of the eleventh hour?

parts.words: Does it come at the end of the eleventh hour
parts.note: the final sixty seconds of the hour before noon or midnight, and also the idiom for a decision taken just in time

explanation.surface: Wondering what arrives at the final moment before a deadline.
explanation.definitionFit: The final sixty-second period before the hour strikes is literally its closing portion, and the phrase also means the latest possible moment.

clue.text: …flier, one appears after 30 seconds

indicators.note: appears after places the second piece following the first

parts.note: thirty seconds is half a minute, and half of the word minute is its first three letters
one is A, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An aircraft that turns up just half a minute late.
explanation.walkthrough: '30 seconds' is half a minute, read as half the word MINUTE, so MIN; 'appears after' sets A behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: The mina, also spelt myna, is an Asian starling known for mimicking speech, a bird and so a flier.

clue.text: Remain undisturbed during stoppage

definitions.meaning: as two words, keep motionless and unmoved
a halt where nothing moves at all

explanation.definitionFit: As two words it means keep motionless; as one word it is a complete halt in activity.

clue.text: Getting together to form work unit in nunnery

indicators.note: in places the unit of work inside the religious house

parts.note: a convent is a house where nuns live
the erg is the CGS unit of work or energy

explanation.surface: Nuns joining to form a working party inside their house.
explanation.walkthrough: The erg is a small physics unit seldom met outside crosswords; 'to form' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Convergent lines or ideas move toward one another until they meet.

clue.text: Jumpy cad?

parts.note: a nervous rotter on the surface, but read as a scoundrel who leaps about, one who goes in for springing

explanation.surface: A nervous scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned British word for a cad is literally also one who leaps or springs.

clue.text: Direction of carriage

definitions.meaning: the way a person holds and carries their body; posture

explanation.definitionFit: A compass heading is a course to steer by, and one's posture or deportment is how one carries oneself.

clue.text: Yes, rust, reddish-brown

annotationWithheld.why: 'Yes, rust, reddish-brown' (7): the anagram of YES RUST has no anagram indicator in the clue as held and as listed in clue databases, so no word signals the rearrangement.

clue.text: Regina got in drier garden tool

indicators.note: got in means entered, so the queen's letter goes inside the drying cloth

parts.note: a towel is something you dry yourself with
Regina, Latin for queen, is abbreviated R as in ER

explanation.surface: The queen climbing into a tumble drier beside her garden tools.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hand implement with a scoop-shaped blade, used for digging in the garden.

clue.text: Mat, German man leaves game

parts.note: a rug is a small floor mat

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so the word man is removed from 'German'

explanation.surface: A German man walks off a mat during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German man' reads as a person, but 'man leaves' tells you to take those three letters out of the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugger is British slang for rugby union football, a team sport.

clue.text: At no time does one puzzle produce harmony

parts.note: at no time means never
one is A, the indefinite article
a crossword is a word puzzle

explanation.surface: Asking whether solving a puzzle never makes anyone content.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produce' is a link; split differently the answer is a phrase meaning no angry word is ever spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Where no quarrelsome word is ever exchanged there is peace and agreement.

clue.text: Sang about alternative back to front garment

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word sang wraps round the reversed piece
back to front means the alternative word is written in reverse order

parts.note: or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A singer performing a number with clothing worn the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' could describe the garment, but it acts only on the little word meaning alternative, which then sits inside 'Sang'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarong is a length of cloth wrapped round the waist, worn in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Grand Egyptian god had meat

parts.note: G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand
Ammon, or Amun, was the chief god of ancient Thebes in Egypt

explanation.surface: A great Egyptian deity once ate meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Gammon is cured or smoked ham, cut from the hind leg of a pig.

clue.text: Street abounding in conflict

parts.note: rife means widespread or abundant

explanation.surface: A road full of fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Strife is bitter disagreement or struggle, a synonym for discord.

clue.text: Quixote's sidekick found in a topless anchorage bar

clue.text: Speak against profits at all times

parts.note: gains are profits
ay, also spelt aye, is an old word for ever or always

explanation.surface: Arguing against profit, always.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to deny or contradict, voicing opposition.

clue.text: Goat in the same place formerly

parts.note: ib, short for ibidem, is Latin for in the same place, used in references
ex means former or formerly, as in an ex-wife

explanation.surface: A goat that used to live in the same spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibex is a wild mountain goat with long curved horns.

clue.text: Regarding morning paper

parts.note: re means about or regarding
a.m. stands for ante meridiem, the morning

explanation.surface: Something about the morning newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A ream is a standard quantity of paper sheets, 480 or 500.

clue.text: Kick up a dust at horse-breeding establishment

indicators.note: kicking something up throws it about, so the letters of dust are scattered

explanation.surface: Raising a fuss at a stable where horses are bred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kick up' rearranges DUST; 'a' and 'at' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a farm where stallions are kept for breeding.

clue.text: Knowing much spinning comets in tandem

indicators.note: spinning means whirling around, so the letters are mixed up
in tandem means two together, one behind the other, so the little word is doubled

explanation.surface: Seeing everything as comets whirl past side by side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in tandem' gives ININ, and 'spinning' mixes it with COMETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Omniscient means all-knowing, having unlimited understanding.

clue.text: Strip of wood from machine unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the machine's name is dropped

parts.note: a lathe is a machine for turning wood or metal

explanation.surface: A thin board taken off a machine before it was done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the final E of LATHE; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lath is a thin flat batten, used under plaster or tiles.

clue.text: Not told about number in military clothes

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the uniform word wraps round the abbreviation

parts.note: dressed in uniform, as soldiers are

explanation.surface: A soldier left in the dark about a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone uninformed has been given no news or facts, so remains in ignorance.
